patch.summary:
Thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — Microsoft Project documents a broader use-case set; Todoist is narrower/specialist.

Frame: General-purpose vs specialist — Microsoft Project documents a broader use-case set; Todoist is narrower/specialist.. Choose Microsoft Project only if your buying job matches “Microsoft 365 project / Planner ladder for Gantt, resources and portfolios — Planner Plan ” rather than Todoist's shape. Choose Todoist only if your buying job matches “Personal and team task manager with natural-language capture — Free; Pro from ~$6.25/user/” rather than Microsoft Project's shape. Workflow advantage: Microsoft Project leans work-management, resource-planning; Todoist leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — Microsoft Project documents a broader use-case set; Todoist is narrower/specialist.
- Positioning: Microsoft Project is Microsoft 365 project / Planner ladder for Gantt, resources and portfolios — Planner Plan 1 from ~$10/user/mo.; Todoist is Personal and team task manager with natural-language capture — Free; Pro from ~$6.25/user/mo annual; Business ~$10..
- Company-size focus: Microsoft Project (mid-market, enterprise) vs Todoist (micro, small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: Microsoft Project-leaning work-management, resource-planning, timeline-reporting vs Todoist-leaning —.
- Researched limits: Microsoft Project — SKU and licensing complexity across Planner/Project plans; Todoist — Not a Work OS or portfolio tool.

Limitations — Microsoft Project: SKU and licensing complexity across Planner/Project plans; Best value assumes Microsoft 365 standardisation; Todoist: Not a Work OS or portfolio tool; Team features mainly on Business.

Poor-fit cases: Microsoft Project is a poor fit when that limitation bites: SKU and licensing complexity across Planner/Project plans · Todoist is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Not a Work OS or portfolio tool · Avoid Microsoft Project if you actually need Todoist's motion (Personal and team task manager with natural-language capture — Free; Pro from ~$)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
